questions.stem: A Pyomo model covers 50 substations and 12 months, and each substation may be inspected in 3 of the months. Its variable is declared over a two-dimensional Set built from the allowed (substation, month) pairs. How many variables does Pyomo create?

options.text: 150, one for each member of the index set
options.says: Right: a Var indexed by a Set gets one variable per member, and the Set holds 50 x 3 allowed pairs, as m.S held 13 allowed starts on tiny.

options.text: 600, one for each pair of the cross product
options.says: The cross product P x Y would give every pair; the sparse Set lists only the allowed ones, 13 of 24 on tiny.

options.text: 62, one for each substation and each month
options.says: A Var indexed by a set of pairs gets one variable per pair, not one per member of each separate set.

options.text: 50, one for each substation, holding its months
options.says: Each member of the Set is a (substation, month) pair and gets its own variable; Pyomo does not group them by substation.

origin.section: Sets Name the Indices, and a Set of Pairs Keeps a Sparse Index Sparse

questions.stem: An analyst builds a model once and wants to lower the 2029 budget and re-solve the same model, with the new value reaching the budget row. How must the budget Param be declared?

options.text: With default=0, so a value can be filled in afterwards
options.says: default= fills indices missing from initialize; a Param without mutable=True is replaced by its number in every row.

options.text: With mutable=True, so it stays a name, not a number
options.says: Right: the row's right side printed as budget[2027], and assigning 1500 changed its value without a rebuild.

options.text: With within=NonNegativeReals, so new values are checked
options.says: within= restricts the values; without mutable=True the row holds the number, so a later assignment cannot reach it.

options.text: With dimen=1, so each year's value can be replaced
options.says: dimen= describes the members of a Set; whether a row can see a new Param value depends only on mutable=True.

origin.section: Params Hold the Data, and a Mutable Param Can Change After the Build

questions.stem: A crew-capacity rule returns sum(hours[j] * x[j, k] for the jobs allowed in month k) <= cap[k], where cap is an ordinary Param. In one month no job is allowed. What happens when Pyomo builds that month's row?

options.text: It writes the row 0 <= cap[k], which always holds
options.says: An empty Python sum is the number 0, so the rule returns True, not a Pyomo row; the lesson's program shows the refusal.

options.text: It skips that month quietly, as Constraint.Skip would
options.says: Only a rule that returns pyo.Constraint.Skip writes no row; a rule that returns True is refused with an error.

options.text: It raises an error about a trivial Boolean
options.says: Right: Pyomo raised InvalidConstraintError, 'resolved to a trivial Boolean (True)'; check for terms and return Constraint.Skip.

options.text: It drops cap[k] and keeps an empty row in the model
options.says: Pyomo does not build a row from a Boolean at all; it raises InvalidConstraintError.

origin.section: A Constraint Rule Writes One Row per Index, and Constraint.Skip Writes None
